# Jubilees Chapter 41 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Judah and Tamar; the twins Perez and Zerah

---

**41:1** And in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the second week, in the second year, Judah took for his son Er the daughter of Shua, and she was of the daughters of Canaan.

**41:2** And Er hated his wife Tamar, for she was not from the daughters of Canaan. And the angel of God killed him because of his wickedness.

**41:3** And Judah said to his second son Onan: "Go in to thy brother's wife and raise up seed for thy brother." But Onan knew that the seed would not be his own, and so he let it fall on the ground whenever he lay with her.

**41:4** And the LORD killed Onan also, for this wickedness.

**41:5** And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: "Remain a widow in thy father's house until my son Shelah is grown." For he feared lest Shelah also should die, as his brothers had died.

**41:6** And Tamar went and remained in her father's house, and she was a widow for many years.

**41:7** And Judah went to shear his sheep in Timnath, and Tamar heard that Judah had gone up. And she put off from her the garments of her widowhood, and she covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself in it and sat by the road toward Timnath.

**41:8** For she saw that Shelah had grown up, and Judah had not given her to him as wife.

**41:9** And Judah saw her and thought she was a harlot. And he turned in to her and said to her: "Let me come in to thee." But she said: "What wilt thou give me that thou mayest come in to me?"

**41:10** And he said: "I will send thee a kid of the goats." And she said: "Give me thy signet and thy cord and thy staff."

**41:11** And he gave them to her. And he came in to her, and she conceived by him.

**41:12** And Tamar arose and went away and laid aside her veil and put on again the garments of her widowhood.

**41:13** And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend Hirah, but he found her not.

**41:14** And he asked the men of the place: "Where is the harlot who sat here on the road?" And they said: "There is no harlot here."

**41:15** And Judah was afraid, for the things he had given her were in her hand, and they were a sign against him. And he said: "Let her keep them, lest we be brought to shame."

**41:16** And when three months had passed, it was told to Judah: "Tamar thy daughter-in-law is with child by whoredom." And Judah said: "Bring her out and let her be burned."

**41:17** And when she was brought out, she sent to Judah saying: "By the man whose these are am I with child." And she said: "Recognize, I pray thee, whose signet and cord and staff these are."

**41:18** And Judah recognized them and said: "She is more righteous than I, for I did not give her Shelah my son." And he did not lie with her again.

**41:19** And she bore twins. One put out his hand first, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on his hand. And he drew back his hand, and his brother came out. And she said: "What a breach thou hast made for thyself!" And his name was called Perez. And afterward his brother came out with the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was called Zerah.

---

*EMET notes: Jubilees' Tamar narrative closely follows Genesis 38 with some compression. The story is notable in Jubilees because it involves intermarriage (Er marries a Canaanite daughter), levirate obligation, and ancestral impurity. Yet Tamar is ultimately declared "more righteous" — Jubilees does not condemn her. "Harlot" follows the Ge'ez term without the "consecrated woman" (qedeshah) distinction present in the Genesis text.*
